Gossiper gives you screen and CV feedback for controls that don't have any of their own — typically an external MIDI foot controller or knob box with no LEDs or display.

Assign one of its parameters to receive the MIDI (or CV, or device control), and Gossiper turns that into a plain CV signal and a pop-up notification on the device screen.

It is an "educated gossiper": it only gossips about a control if you're actually looking at it. A pop-up appears only on a device screen page that has one of Gossiper's four Assign to notify slots addressed to it, because MOD devices only show a pop-up for a plugin whose parameter is linked to a control (a knob or a footswitch) that is currently visible on the screen.

Good to know

Gossiper has no audio inputs or outputs, so it doesn't sit in your signal chain. Place it anywhere on the pedalboard. The CV outputs, the display on the plugin and the pop-ups are three independent ways of using the same control: you can use any of them, and the outputs keep working when the pop-ups cannot (an old firmware, a MOD Duo).

Sample demonstration of the plugin in action
01

Plugin GUI overview

Item Description Interactivity
A — Display Says which control was used last and what it did: Footswitch 2 — ON, or Pot 3 — 63%. It stays on, and lights up for a moment each time a control is used. This is how you see a message on a device that has no screen for plugin pop-ups, such as the MOD Duo. Only visualization status
B — Footswitch indicator A disc in a colour of its own for each footswitch. Lit while the footswitch is ON, and mirrored on CV Output N (0 V / 10 V). The one used last is outlined. Only visualization status. Clicking on it does nothing.
C — Footswitch label Click and type a name (up to 15 characters): this is the text the pop-up and the display show for that footswitch. Editable field
D — Potentiometer The position of the knob (0–100 %) as a meter, and the CV range (Minimum–Maximum, in volts) its 0–10 V output is scaled into. The one used last is outlined. Only visualization status. To change the range, open the settings.
E — Settings Opens the settings page (section 3). The gear icon above the plugin opens it too. Button
F — CV outputs 1–7 are the footswitches and P1–P4 the potentiometers. Jacks
02

What it's for

A MIDI foot controller (say, a cheap "Chocolate"-style box) can send Program Change or CC messages, but usually has no LED to confirm whether a patch is currently on or off, and no screen to show a knob's value. Gossiper closes that loop:

  1. Assign a Footswitch N or Potentiometer N parameter to receive that MIDI message (or a CV signal, or a device knob/footswitch).
  2. Assign one of the 4 Assign to notify N parameters to a page/knob or footswitch slot on the device screen.
  3. Use the CV output. CV Foot - Out N (footswitches) or CV Pot - Out N (potentiometers) now carries a plain, calibrated CV signal you can route into any other plugin's CV-addressable parameter — the same way you would with a "Control to CV" utility plugin.

From then on, every time that MIDI controller sends a message, you see it confirmed on the device screen — without needing to look down at an unlit external box.

03

Setting it up on the device

The shortest path

Open the settings page, tap Assign next to Footswitch 1 and press the button of your controller; then tap Assign next to Pop-up slot 1 and pick a knob or footswitch of the page you play from. Press the button again: its name pops up on the device screen, the disc lights up on the plugin and CV Foot - Out 1 goes to 10 V. The steps below show each tap.

Click Settings (or the gear icon above the plugin) to open the settings page. It has one panel for each thing you can link, and each panel starts with Hardware assignment: that is the step where you choose which control of your device, your MIDI foot controller or your pedal drives that parameter.

On a small screen the page splits into several pages instead of scrolling: use the arrows in the top bar (they are always there), the dots between them, or swipe sideways on a touch screen.

Step 1 — Assign the control. In Footswitches, find a row that is not used yet — or, in Potentiometers, a row for a knob — and tap Assign next to it.

In the opened modal, select MIDI option in Assign to.

Now you must send the MIDI message (or pick the device control) you want to drive it. After it, save. The button shows a check mark once it is assigned.

Step 2 — Assign a pop-up slot. Do the same for one of the four slots in Screen pop-ups — this is what decides where the pop-up will show.

Step 3 — Choose the target. Pick what the slot is addressed to — usually Device, so it lives on the screen itself.

Step 4 — Pick the page and control. Choose which page (and which knob or footswitch, B/C) the slot sits on. Whenever that page is showing, that's where the pop-up appears.

Repeat step 1 for as many footswitches/potentiometers as you're feeding in, and steps 2–4 for as many slots as you want pages covered by — up to 4, so you can get a pop-up whichever of up to 4 pages you're currently on.

The page also lets you type the name of each footswitch and the Min and Max voltage of each potentiometer, and keeps your own presets (Saved presets).

No screen for pop-ups? The MOD Duo (and any device without the HMI) cannot show pop-ups: the display on the plugin itself (item A, section 1) is the feedback there. Open the pedalboard and look at it.

04

How the pop-up decides when to appear

  • Footswitches gossip immediately — the pop-up shows the footswitch's custom label the instant it flips, styled inverted when turning ON and normal when turning OFF.
  • Potentiometers gossip once you stop — the pop-up shows Pot N — xx% a short moment after the value settles, so sweeping a knob doesn't spam a message on every intermediate step.
  • No assignment, no pop-up. If none of the 4 notify slots is currently addressed to a visible page, Gossiper stays silent.

Requires MOD Dwarf firmware v1.13 or newer for the pop-up mechanism. On older firmware the CV outputs still work; you just won't get the on-screen message.

Note from the author: the pop-up is meant for occasional confirmation, not as a live debugging readout — don't expect to use it for something that changes every few milliseconds.

05

Renaming a footswitch

Click a footswitch's label field and type a new name (up to 15 characters). Allowed characters are letters, digits, spaces and + - : _ .; anything else is replaced with _. The name is what the pop-up shows for that footswitch, and it's saved with the pedalboard/preset.

06

Why bother: one real example

Gossiper can also replace stacks of "Control to CV" utility plugins: one Gossiper with several footswitches and potentiometers assigned does the job of many single-purpose CV converters, at a fraction of the CPU cost.

For instance, a forum user reported that, after replacing those plugins with Gossiper, the Dwarf's CPU usage went down from 81% to 72%.

07

Tips

Name the footswitches after what they do

The pop-up shows the label, so Drive or Solo says more on a screen than Footswitch 3. Rename them before you assign the controller, and you will recognise the message without counting buttons.

One notify slot per page you play from

A pop-up shows only while the control you addressed to a slot is visible. If you play from two pages of the device, address a second slot to a control on the other page, and so on up to four.

Footswitch and CV in one go

A footswitch that Gossiper receives is also CV Foot - Out N (0 V off, 10 V on). Address a plugin's On/Off to that output and a MIDI button turns the plugin on, with the name on the screen. The feedback and the action come from the same control.

Tame the range of a knob

A potentiometer reaches its CV output scaled into Minimum–Maximum volts. Set Minimum 2 to 2 V and Maximum 2 to 6 V and the whole sweep of the knob moves a parameter between 20 % and 60 % of a 0–10 V range, without losing resolution on the knob.

Do not use it as a meter

The pop-up of a potentiometer waits for the value to settle, so it is for confirming a position, not for watching a value change continuously. Use the display on the plugin for that.

08

Questions & answers

The pop-up never appears.

Check, in this order: (1) the control that sent the message is assigned to a Footswitch N or Pot N parameter; (2) one Assign to notify slot is addressed to a control of the device; (3) that control is visible on the screen right now (it is the page the device is showing); (4) the firmware is MOD Dwarf v1.13 or newer. The CV outputs and the display on the plugin work without any of these.

Does it work on the MOD Duo and the MOD Duo X?

The plugin loads and the CV outputs work on both. The MOD Duo has no screen for plugin pop-ups, so the display on the plugin (open the pedalboard in the browser) is where you see the last control used. Pop-ups need the HMI of the Dwarf.

Is it stereo? Does it add latency?

Neither question applies: Gossiper has no audio ports. It only turns what it receives into control voltages.

Can I invert a knob with Min and Max?

No. The two values are put in order, so Minimum 8 V and Maximum 2 V give the same range as 2 V and 8 V. To invert a control, use a plugin that does it on the CV.

Why can't I turn the footswitch indicator on by clicking it?

The disc only shows what the footswitch received. Gossiper reports on a control that lives elsewhere; to change it, use the controller, or the parameter in the plugin's own addressing.

Are the names saved?

Yes. The label of each footswitch is saved with the pedalboard and with the plugin presets.

09

Port reference

Port Type Description
CV Foot - Out 1–4, CV Output 5–7 CV output 0 V / 10 V, mirrors Footswitch N (the first four have the longer name).
Footswitch 1–7 Control input (toggle) Assign this to receive MIDI/CV/device input.
Assign to notify 1–4 Control input No audio/CV effect; assign to a device page/control so pop-ups show there.
Pot 1–4 Control input (0–1) Assign this to receive MIDI/CV/device input.
Minimum N / Maximum N Control input (volts) The CV range Potentiometer N's 0–1 value is scaled into.
CV Pot - Out 1–4 CV output Potentiometer N scaled into [Minimum N, Maximum N] volts.
Footswitch label 1–7 Plugin property (patch) The custom name for each footswitch, edited from the GUI text field.
